concepts.title: Watercolour
concepts.shortDescription: Soft washes and visible paper texture.
concepts.whyItMatters: Soft edges create a gentle, handmade feeling.

concepts.title: Negative space
concepts.shortDescription: Leave breathing room around the main subject.
concepts.whyItMatters: An uncluttered area guides attention and leaves room for text.
promptExamples: generous negative space around the subject

concepts.title: Rule of thirds
concepts.shortDescription: Place the subject away from the centre.
concepts.whyItMatters: An off-centre focal point can give the scene movement.
promptExamples: subject positioned on the left third

concepts.title: Low angle
concepts.shortDescription: Look up at the subject from below.
concepts.whyItMatters: The subject can feel larger or more powerful.

concepts.title: Wide shot
concepts.shortDescription: Show the subject within a wider environment.
concepts.whyItMatters: The setting and scale become part of the story.
promptExamples: wide shot showing the surrounding environment

concepts.title: Soft light
concepts.shortDescription: Use broad, gentle light with soft shadows.
concepts.whyItMatters: Gentle transitions reveal shape without harsh contrast.
promptExamples: soft side lighting with gentle shadows

concepts.title: Rim light
concepts.shortDescription: Light the edge of the subject from behind.
concepts.whyItMatters: A lit edge helps separate the subject from its background.
promptExamples: subtle warm rim light along the silhouette

concepts.title: Limited palette
concepts.shortDescription: Choose a small family of colours.
concepts.whyItMatters: A few colours make the image feel cohesive.
promptExamples: limited palette of warm orange and cool blue

concepts.title: Muted colour
concepts.whyItMatters: Quiet colours can support a calm or nostalgic mood.

concepts.title: Shape language
concepts.shortDescription: Use rounded or angular shapes deliberately.
concepts.whyItMatters: Rounded shapes often feel approachable; angular ones can feel tense.
promptExamples: rounded shapes and a clear friendly silhouette

concepts.title: Cinematic illustration
concepts.shortDescription: Frame a scene as a moment in a story.
concepts.whyItMatters: Lighting and framing help create narrative atmosphere.

concepts.title: Material texture
concepts.whyItMatters: Surface detail can make objects feel tactile and distinct.
promptExamples: matte ceramic surfaces with subtle texture

recipes.title: A character with a story
recipes.summary: Connect a character, a place, and one lighting choice.

recipes.title: Room for a message
recipes.summary: Make a poster illustration with space for your own typography.

intent.subject: a single wildflower
intent.constraints: Leave the upper half empty; no lettering.

recipes.title: A tactile object
recipes.summary: Explore how light describes a simple material.

exercises.title: Change only the light
exercises.summary: Compare a gentle scene with a stronger silhouette.
exercises.objective: Create two versions of the same prompt. Keep the subject and framing fixed; replace soft light with rim light. Which separates the subject more clearly?
exercises.starterPrompt: A small robot standing in a dark train station.

exercises.title: Let the setting tell the story
exercises.summary: Explore how framing changes a scene.
exercises.objective: Compare a low-angle medium shot with a wide shot. Keep everything else fixed. Notice which gives the environment more importance.
exercises.starterPrompt: A tiny explorer beside an enormous ceramic cup.
